full_judgment:
11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner today has filed a supplementary affidavit and has taken ground No.10, 11, 12 and 13 in continuation of his grounds taken earlier in substantive Revisional Application and supporting the grounds very candidly submits that the Appellate Court has not at all reversed the finding of the Trial Court as to bringing of any witness to support basic contention of the plaintiff as to the creditors and also failed to appreciate the exhibit Ga(1) the application for correcting the S.A. Khatian contending that the schedule as stated in the application was not annexed with the application though the Trial court has recorded specific findings on those issues but the Appellate court has totally failed to reverse those findings and thus committed fundamental error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 13. On the other hand Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the Senior counsel along with Mr. Serajur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing before this court in countering the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner has strait way submitted that the basic question raised before this court as to whether 2 registered Debuttemama were acted upon during the life time of Ramoni Mohan Das Baishnabi and whether, the plaintiff is only serving heir of the said Ramoni Mohan Das and contended further that nature of the deeds also have to be cor_6idered before considering the oral evidence. He submits that the Appellate Court has clearly found that the deeds though executed by Ramoni Mohan were never been acted upon and held on consideration of the evidence both oral and documentary and the plaintiffs is the only surviving heir of late Ramoni Mohan, the Appellate Court since settled the facts being a final court of facts, these warrant no interference by the Hon'ble court and thereby, the Appellate Court committed no error of law in reversing findings of the Trial court. He further contends that on the face of the deeds, it is to be further decided and held, whether the two documents are "Illusory" endowments and also to be considered the evidence in that angle and in order to arrive at such conclusion the court has to consider the behavior of dedicator and the evidence in as much as Ramoni Mohan during his life time got recorded his name in S.A. Khatian (exhibit-2, 2(ka), 2(kha) and 2(Chaa) and sold land vide exhibit No.7 treating the properties as personal and secular properties and to ascertain such facts, the documentary evidence were not properly considered by the Trial Court but the Appellate Court has considered those aspect on the basis of the evidence both oral and documentary of the case and legally reversed the findings of the Trial court and committed no error of law. Referring to exhibit-14, it has been submitted that in a suit for realization of arrear rent filed Rent Suit No.44 of 1958 by Sree Mati Braja Bala Baishnabi and another, and the Munsif Court, Sylhet came to the findings :- "The plaintiff' have exhibited a debattaranama Ext.-I, the perusal of which shows that this property along with other properties, was gifted to deity but Exts. A-B a decree and copy of plaint in R.S. 182/52, show that donor Ramoni Mohan dealt with this property as his private property long, long after the execution of debatturnama. Thus it is clear that subsequent conduct of donor shows that debatturnama was not acted upon. So 1 am convinced that plaintiffs have no locustandi to bring this suit on the basis of debatturnama which was not acted upon." Against the said judgment the plaintiff Shebait Braja Bala took appeal before the District Judge, Sylhet being No.16 of 1959 (Ext.15). The appeal was heard by the Second Additional Court of Subordinate Judge, who affirmed the judgment of the Trial Court holding "The learned Trail Court accepted the defendant's contention as of substance and held that the Debuttarnarna Ext.-1 was not acted upon. 1 also find nothing to differ from him. Exhibits A and B conclusively proves the defendant's contention that Ramoni Mohan even after executing Debuttarnama in the year 1351 B.S. in respect of the jama and holding in brought Rent Suit No.182 of 1952 in respect of same jama and holding in his individual capacity giving an absolute go-bye to Ext.]. This shows clearly that this Ext.1 was not acted upon nor was it meant to be acted upon by Ramoni Mohan even during his life time "This contention- of the tenant, defdts was corroborated to the fullest extent by plff. No.2. But 1 may observe here that there is an apparent clash of interest between plff. No.1 and plff. No.2 and for that purpose I would like to leave the question of title of plff. No.1 and 2 interest open for a decision in a properly constituted suit between them as there is no scope for any finding of their title in the present suit or appeal." Referring to exhibit-7, the learned counsel submitted that the Trial Court committed error of law in finding contrary to the recital of the deed in as much as the Trial Court without considering the original deed has drawn conclusion on surmises but in fact Ramoni Mohan executed deed on 11.2.1952 and the schedule of both the deeds indicated that the preliminary number remains the same and in view of such facts the Appellate Court upon discharging the entire evidence held that the deeds were not acted upon and thus committed no error of law. He further contends that from exhibit-"Uma" it would be evident that the last alleged Shebait had come to Sylhet but did not convene meeting but the Hindu locals allegedly held the meeting on 23.5.1972 and in the meeting the alleged committee for the management of the property was formed and for the self same property the plaintiff filed suit before 1972 and the plaintiff was not notified while convened the meeting by the locals which is also evident from the exhibit "Uma" and alleged committee admittedly had formed in the absence of the plaintiff and this vital aspect of the case has not been considered by the Trial Court. The learned Counsel further submitted that from the evidence of the DWs it has been indicated that "idol" / deities had been shifted to house of the Secretary, the alleged Shebait and the Shebait is residing in his personal property and thus public has got no excess there. It would be evident further from the evidence that the alleged deitie's house of Akhara Bari has got no existence, what so ever, in spite of such evidence on record, such basic point, the Trial Court has not at all considered but this vital aspect of the case has been thoroughly considered by the Appellate Court and held that the deities have no existence and consequently, held that the deeds were not acted upon and therefore, committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned counsel further submitted that the plaintiff is not bound by any action of the alleged committee to have taken after the filing of the suit in 1969 and such actions are bad in law and suffers from principle of Lis pendens, as completed under section 52 of the Transfer Property Act and the alleged recording of name of the alleged Shebait after 1969 has got no validity and as such, the plaintiff is not bound by such recording allegedly made in the name of the alleged deities, but such aspect of the case was not considered by the Trial Court. He submitted further that natural corollary is that admittedly the plaintiff is the only heir of Ramoni Mohan and after the death of Ramoni automatically, the title and the possession of the property had vested on the plaintiff, if no contrary title is established by producing any legal evidence and accordingly, the name of the plaintiff was recorded in the S.A. Khatian and paid the rents denying the existence of the deities, 

 16. On perusal of the judgment of the Appellate Court, it transpires that the Appellate Court has reversed the findings and decision of the Trial Court and held that the dedication to have made by 2 documents by Ramoni Mohan had not been acted upon as the donor had not completely divested himself of all beneficial interest in the property given in endowment and that the plaintiff is the legal heir of the said Ramoni Mohan and he has interest in the land and further held perusing the exhibits, in as much as the judgments of the litigations have expressly disclosed that Ramoni Mohan Das during his life time realized rent from the tenants and also for arrear of rents had filed rent suits and his name also was recorded in S.A. Khatian which is evident from exhibit-Gha(1) and further that such recording of rights has not been challenged 

 18. The Appellate Court has held relying upon mainly on the S.A. Khatian exhibit 2-2('), sale deed dated 22/02/1952 exhibit 7 and order dated 5.1.1959 in rent suit no.44 of 1958 and also on the basis of the order passed in Rent appeal No.16 of 1959 (arose out of rent suit no.44 of 1958) that the plaintiff has been able to prove that during the life time of said Ramoni Mohan, he did not divest himself from the properties rather he mutated his name and realized rent. The A"ppellate Court also held that the plaintiff is admittedly the grand son of Ramoni Mohan and the title and possession naturally had vested in him. He also found that the deities were not kept in the Debuttar properties but allegedly preserved in the custody of the Secretary of the committee in his personal house and also found that alleged application made by Ramoni Mohan contained no schedule of the property and as such, recording of names in S.A. Khatian remained unchallenged and I am of the view that the Appellate Court has decided the matter to its true perspective considering the evidence both oral and documentary and law and in reversing the findings, it appears further that the Appellate Court has committed no error of law. I have also concentrated myself as to whether the deeds ' were acted upon and upon scrutiny found that the original maker of the deeds i.e. Ramoni Mohan had recorded his name in S.A. Khatian during his life time and Braja Bala tried to establish herself as the Shebait by filing rent suit but the Munsif, 1st Court, Sylhet in rent suit no.44 of 1958 which had clearly held that the deeds were not acted upon and such findings were affirmed by the Appellate Court with the opinion that in an appropriate constituted suit the fate of the deeds will be decided and accordingly, the plaintiff had filed the suit in 1969. It appears from the resolution of the meeting held on 23.5.1972 Braja Bala was not present. The life of the committee appears to have given by the learned District Judge till appointment of the Shebait and since the plaintiff has been able to prove that the dedication of properties made by Ramoni Mohan by 2 deeds were not acted upon and further held that the function of the committee thereby ceased and in holding as such, the Appellate Court has committed no error of law. It is in evidence that the del'ies are not being maintained in the land of the Debuttar property but kept in a private house of the Secretary and as such, the very purpose of dedication as it appears to have lost and as such, I am of the opinion that the plaintiff has been able to prove that the Endowments had been made were "Illusory endowments and "Illusory endowments" are sham endowments. In such endowment the donor does not completely divest himself of all beneficial interest in the property given in endowment.
